summary: Installed the typesafe-ai skill into the gizmo project via `npx skills add typesafe-ai/skills --skill typesafe-ai --agent '*' -y --json`, verified it with `skills list --json`, and read the TypeSafe docs index (https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt) to load the Jev/System One skill content. After the user asked to evaluate all non-empty transcripts and journals under gizmo and `~/UnityProjects/ncp/` for prompting/model-choice/skill-usage issues, the assistant began the survey by spawning four parallel subagents to inspect gizmo journals, Unity projects (ncp and siblings), global agent histories plus TypeSafe readiness, and to read SKILL.md for Jev question design.
decisions: Used the npx skills method (with `--agent '*' -y --json`) instead of the Claude plugin method, because the runtime is not Claude Code (it's Gizmo/pi); chose non-interactive flags to skip the agent-selection prompt.

Treated https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt as the live source of truth for TypeSafe, per SKILL.md, and resolved to keep rules/calculations in code while putting semantic judgment in narrow typed questions.

Chose to evaluate transcripts/journals across gizmo and `~/UnityProjects/ncp/` (and sibling Unity projects) rather than just one location, by spawning parallel survey subagents rather than a single sequential scan.

Spawned four parallel subagents to divide the survey work: gizmo journals, Unity projects (ncp + siblings), global agent histories + TypeSafe readiness, and SKILL.md-driven Jev question design — rather than doing the survey inline.
errors: First `display` tool call failed validation because the `spec` parameter was passed as a stringified JSON string instead of an object literal.
Second `display` call failed validation because the `spec` property was missing entirely (only a `title` was provided).
